_README: Single source for the value-free SCREEN/window-label rules (ADR-0024 §6a/§6b). A window title and a window-title-derived step prefix routinely embed the case value ('Salesforce - Order #10900', 'Create INC0010010 | Incident | ServiceNow'); these rules strip the embedded record numbers / id tokens so the SAME logical screen collapses to one node at the screen grain and the SAME step-type collapses across cases at the element grain. Distinct from process-label-patterns.json, which strips value TAILS off a step name; these strip embedded record tokens ANYWHERE in a window/screen string. Consumed by BOTH viewer/process-map-levels.js (screenType: the screen-grain key/label) and normalization/step_suggest.py (the window-title-derived step-name prefix _short_app) so the two agree -- no hand-synced regex to drift. Rules are applied IN ORDER, each a GLOBAL replace (unlike process-label's first-rule-wins); the consumer then trims leading/trailing separators. `replacement` uses JS String.replace style; the Python loader maps it through. The id rule is UPPERCASE-LED on purpose so lowercase alnum codes that ARE the screen/app name (e.g. SAP 'va01') survive, while record ids (INC0010009, CUST-10852, SO12) are stripped. The colon-prose rule drops a trailing ': <3+ words>' -- the dominant pattern for a title that embeds FREE-TEXT field content ('TAMBA - Resolution: ATM down on arrival' -> 'TAMBA - Resolution'), which no record-id strip can catch -- while a short sub-screen ('Settings: Privacy') is left intact; it is anchored to the LAST colon (the tail has no inner colon). Keep it dependency-free JSON.
